messages:
Priya Singh: Hey team — kicking off SilkRoad private deploy handoff. Customer finished infra provisioning but we still need final confirmations on network egress, IAM roles, KMS key access, and audit log forwarding. Low tolerance window — they want week0 cutover next Tue. Can owners chime in with checklists?
Ethan Liu: I can take network. Quick ask: do we have the full list of outbound CIDRs they will originate from, or are we still using their peered VPC ranges? Need port list for egress policy.
Priya Singh: They gave two peered ranges (10.40.0.0/16 and 10.41.0.0/16). They asked us to whitelist Redwood public egress for telemetry and image pulls.
Ethan Liu: OK. For runtime egress we require these destinations (to be whitelisted on their firewall):
```
- 34.82.120.0/24 (redwood-registry-us)
- 52.23.45.0/24 (metadata/telemetry-us)
- 13.224.0.0/14 (model-artifacts-cdn)
- TCP 443 outbound to *.redwood-inference.com
```
Also recommend allowing NTP (UDP 123) to our NTP service and DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver.
Marisol Ramos: Noted. From CS side: SilkRoad flagged that delays on audit log forwarding are a renewal risk. They want assurance that Splunk streaming will be validated prior to cutover. Can SRE validate ingestion SLA?
Priya Singh: Yep. Add action: validate Splunk HEC token routing and retention settings. Who owns that?
Kai Nakamura: Security here. KMS details: SilkRoad will bring their customer-managed KMS key in AWS (alias/aws/redwood-silkroad-cmk). We need: 1) a key policy granting Redwood Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey with condition on AWS:SourceAccount = <their-account-id>, 2) a key rotation schedule (annual OK, but mention if they have auto-rotate). Also: confirm whether HSM-backed key required (they said yes in the contract).
Priya Singh: They did mark "HSM-backed key" as required. Marisol, can you confirm they requested annual rotation or customer-managed rotation?
Marisol Ramos: Confirmed — customer wants annual rotation but to manage it themselves. They asked Redwood not to rotate without notice. That's a stick on the contract.
Ethan Liu: Small note on IAM roles: we'll need an assume-role ARN in their account for the inference runtime to pull models and push metrics. Suggested role trust policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-cross-account"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Condition": {}
    }
  ]
}
```
We'll share exact REDWOOD_ACCOUNT ID once infra ticket picks up. Also need kms:Decrypt permissions for that role.
Priya Singh: Great. For audit logs: SilkRoad uses Splunk HEC in us-east-1 with a 7-day warm retention and 365-day cold. They want logs forwarded from our private control plane and from the inference nodes. Is there a sample syslog/hec payload we can hand them for validation?
Kai Nakamura: Yes — we'll send a minimal HEC payload example and an ingestion checklist. Also: ensure logs contain request_id, model_version, and user agent. That is required for their audit compliance.
Priya Singh: Action items recap: 1) Ethan — provide finalized egress/ports + test IP allowlist by EOD tomorrow. 2) Kai — send KMS key policy template and HEC payload + ingestion checklist. 3) Marisol — confirm contractual note about rotation and schedule a call with their security owner. 4) SRE — validate Splunk ingestion and produce a smoke test runbook.
Marisol Ramos: Adding one more: raise a renewal-risk flag in Gainsight if Splunk validation slips past Friday. I'll draft the note. :warning:
Ethan Liu: Will run a quick smoke using their peer ranges and post results here. ETA: 24h. :white_check_mark:
sre-bot: smoke-test: splunk-hec-ingest -> queued. Run id: r-2026-3421. You will get results in this thread when complete.
Priya Singh: Thanks all. If nothing blocks, I'll schedule the cutover dress rehearsal for Monday 14:00 PT and invite SilkRoad + infra contacts. If blockers appear, we'll push and notify.
Marisol Ramos: I'll prep the customer-facing document summarizing these asks and the risk implications. Expect a draft in ~3 hours.
Ethan Liu: FYI — quick config snippet for their firewall team (can paste into their rule UI):
```
allow from 10.40.0.0/16,10.41.0.0/16 to 34.82.120.0/24 tcp 443
allow from 10.40.0.0/16,10.41.0.0/16 to 52.23.45.0/24 tcp 443
allow ntp udp 123 to redwood-ntp.example.com
```
Priya Singh: Perfect. Closing loop — I'll post the meeting invite after the dress rehearsal time is confirmed. Thanks :pray:
